title: Border K9 sniffs out 99 pounds of prohibited meat, plants and monitor lizard in suitcase from Thailand
text:
K9 Maisy discovered 50 pounds of raw meat, mangoes and 16 pounds of Bengal monitor lizard in luggage from Thailand, prompting a wildlife seizure.

K9 Maisy alerted officers to the bag, which contained 50 pounds of meat, including raw meat, 33 pounds of mangoes, garlic, bamboo, banana plants and approximately 16 pounds of Bengal"If you discovered all this in a suitcase, wouldn't you be this happy?
" CBP wrote alongside a photo of Maisy posing behind the unusual haul. CBP agriculture detector dog Maisy poses behind prohibited meat, plants and wildlife products seized from luggage arriving from Thailand during an inspection by U.S. Customs and Border Protection. CBP agriculture specialists routinely inspect international luggage for prohibited meat, plants and wildlife products that can introduce pests, animal diseases or invasive species into the United States.
Fish and Wildlife said officers working with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration inspected a vehicle at the San Ysidro Port of Entry and found approximately 436 fish, including rockfish, lingcod, sheephead and yellowtail. A California Department of Fish and Wildlife officer examines fish seized during an inspection at the San Ysidro Port of Entry as part of an investigation into the alleged illegal importation of fish from Mexico.
